I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It has no lodash import left, and the exported signatures are unchanged. I haven't run it against inputs or compared its output with the original's.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 229 bytes (min+gzip), with 114 bytes of your own code. The type check on `out/module.ts` alone (strict mode) passed. The project-wide `tsc` run still reports errors on `src/module.ts` (missing `lodash/keyBy` and `lodash/fromPairs` modules), so I couldn't build or size the original for comparison. I don't know how 114 bytes compares with the original's own-code size. The unmigrated `src/module.ts` is still in place.

- **`doubled`:** `mapValues` from `es-toolkit`, with the same callback.
- **`byNameKey`:** `keyBy` from `es-toolkit` takes a function instead of lodash's `'name'` shorthand, so I pass `(row) => row.name`. Duplicate names keep the last row, as before.
- **`toLookup`:** es-toolkit has no `fromPairs` outside `es-toolkit/compat`. The compat version bundled to 313 bytes, so I built it from two core calls instead: `mapValues(keyBy(pairs, (p) => p[0]), (p) => p[1])`. With overlapping names the last pair wins, as lodash's `fromPairs` does.

The two-call `toLookup` adds a little of your own code (114 bytes against 95 with the compat version). In exchange the bundle is about 84 bytes smaller (229 against 313).
